sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, password_hash, role, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email: unique — login lookup by email (auth service); employee_number: unique — natural key; manager_id: findByManagerId direct-report scoping
table leave_types | fields: code, name, requires_approval, max_consecutive_days, is_paid | pk: code | indexes: code: natural key / PK — static catalog lookup by LeaveTypeCode

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type_code, policy_name, annual_entitlement_days, accrual_period_months, carry_forward_days, min_notice_days, max_request_days, requires_manager_approval, effective_from, effective_to, status | pk: id | fks: leave_type_code -> leave_types.code | indexes: leave_type_code: findByLeaveTypeCode / effective-policy selection

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end, entitled_days, used_days, pending_days | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code | indexes: (employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end): unique — findByKey at-most-one-row invariant; employee_id: per-employee balance reads

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date, end_date, requested_days, reason, status, approver_id, approval_comment, submitted_at, decided_at, cancelled_by, cancelled_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code; approver_id -> employees.id; cancelled_by -> employees.id | indexes: (employee_id, status): list scoping by owner/status; (leave_type_code, start_date): date-range + type filtering
data_notes:
This feature introduces NO new repository interfaces or concrete implementations — the seed is a knex seed (seeds/ directory) that writes development-only demo data directly via the knex client, not through the runtime repository layer. GP-001 (repository pattern) governs services/controllers, not one-shot dev seed scripts; the seed is idempotent via existence checks (e.g. `where({ email })` / `where({ code })` before insert, or `onConflict().ignore()`), so re-running never duplicates rows or fails.

The seed reuses the EXISTING conceptual tables (already defined in the codebase and reproduced above for completeness): employees, leave_types, leave_policies, leave_balances, leave_requests. No schema changes, no new columns, no new tables. The seed must populate: (1) one manager + one employee with bcrypt password_hash minted by the same bcrypt call the auth service verifies with (bcrypt.hashSync, cost 10); (2) the leave_types and leave_policies the balance logic needs; (3) a leave_balance for the CURRENT accrual period for each employee (period derived via the shared periodContaining helper, not hand-written dates); (4) two or three leave_requests in different states.

Seeded dates are calendar dates in UTC (the existing UTC discipline). The seed is wired into knexfile.js development environment only and must never run as part of migrate.

transactionContract is left EMPTY: the seed is a one-shot dev script with no caller-controlled unit-of-work boundary. If atomicity is desired, the seed wraps its inserts in knex's own `knex.transaction(...)` (knex seeds run in a transaction by default), but this is not a data-access-layer contract the runtime repositories participate in.

open_questions.question: Should the seed keep leave_balances counters (pending_days/used_days) consistent with the seeded leave_requests' states, or seed requests purely for list/detail display with zeroed counters?
open_questions.impact: The reservation lifecycle (submit increments pending_days; approve decrements pending_days and increments used_days) is binding across the app. If the seed inserts a SUBMITTED/APPROVED request without adjusting the matching balance row, GET /balances/me will report available = entitled_days - 0 - 0 (full entitlement) while the list/detail pages show reserved/used days — an internally inconsistent demo dataset.
candidate_options: Seed requests in DRAFT/APPROVED/REJECTED states only and adjust used_days for APPROVED (no SUBMITTED, so no pending_days reservation needed)
Seed requests in multiple states AND replicate the reservation arithmetic into pending_days/used_days so balances stay consistent
Seed requests purely for display and leave balance counters at zero (accept the inconsistency)

transaction_contract: The seed is a one-shot development script with no caller-controlled unit-of-work boundary; no runtime repository participates. Leave EMPTY per the read-only/single-write guidance — the seed's own atomicity (if any) is knex's built-in per-seed transaction, not a cross-cutting data-access contract.
